correctness.rationale: For all a,b,c,d>=1 on binary linear word 0^a1^b0^c1^d, a minimal absent contiguous word x is exactly a missing factor with both length-|x|-1 prefix and suffix present; this implies every proper factor present. Reconstruct one-run forbidden powers and two-run downward-closed factor rectangles, the forced full inner exponents in three-run factors, and the two possible four-run shapes. Five or more-run candidates fail a boundary deletion condition. Each of the displayed ten disjoint word families follows by these necessary-and-sufficient tests. Counting yields |A(T)|=b+c+(1+[a>c])(1+[d>b]); the two comparison flags factor as independent weighted pair generating functions F0=uz²/((1-uz)(1-uz²)), F1=uz³/((1-z)(1-uz²)), giving uF0²+2u²F0F1+u⁴F1². At fixed length n, n-1 is the maximum except the unique n=6 word (2,1,1,2) up to alphabet exchange attains n. Independently programmed all factors and every minimality test (NOT using submitted verify.py), obtaining exact set equality for 1,090 positive quadruples with length <=17, including equal-run and extreme comparisons; finite test corroborates the proof but is not proof of all positive lengths.
